description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  Data::Dumper is on the README's infrastructure list.

REPRODUCER, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on the same file:

    require re;
    print re::is_regexp(qr/x/) ? 1 : 0, "\n";

    perl: 1
    PCL : Undefined subroutine &RE::is_regexp called

`require re` SUCCEEDS under PCL (the core `re.pm` loads); what is absent is the
function, which real perl installs from `universal.c` / `re.xs`.

WHERE IT BITES.  `Data/Dumper.pm:324`:

    if ( $realpack and ($] >= 5.009005 ? re::is_regexp($val) : â¦) ) {

so EVERY call to `Dumper` on a blessed structure reaches it.  Measured on the
Data-Dumper-2.183-0 dist (s481b): PCL 19 PASS / 2 PARTIAL / 5 FAIL, 406 ok / 66
not-ok, against perl's 25 PASS / 829 ok / 0.  Four of the files die at row 1 or
2 with this message â `t/bless.t` (perl 11 rows, PCL 1), `t/bugs.t` (24 â 1),
`t/freezer.t` (8 â 0), `t/freezer_useperl.t` (7 â 0) â and `t/qr.t` fails one
step later with "Can't handle 'Regexp' type", which is the same question asked
of the dumper's own dispatch.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a).  `re::is_regexp` asks a question about the BOX
representation ("is this SV a compiled regex?"), which is the class the s377
ruling put behind the `builtin::` shim-dispatch seam.  In plain Perl the
common case is `ref($_[0]) eq 'Regexp'`, so a `lib/` shim can carry it â but
note that PCL currently loads the REAL core `re.pm`, and a `lib/re.pm` would
SHADOW the pragma (`use re 'taint'`, `use re 'debug'`, `use re
'/xism'`).  Whoever takes this must decide between (a) a `lib/re.pm` that
reimplements the pragma's no-op behaviour as well, and (b) supplying just the
function so the core `re.pm` keeps the pragma.  Measure which spellings of
`use re` occur before choosing.

BAR: guard rows with perl as the oracle for `re::is_regexp` on a qr//, on a
plain ref, on a string and on undef, plus a `Dumper` round trip over a blessed
structure and a qr//; whichever way the pragma question goes, `use re 'taint'`
must still be accepted.  A `lib/` change owes the full sweep.
subject: `re::is_regexp` is missing, and it is the top cause of Data::Dumper's own test suite: four files (bless.t, bugs.t, freezer.t, freezer_useperl.t) die "Undefined subroutine &RE::is_regexp called" at the first structure they dump.
